response.sql: WITH film_copies AS (SELECT f.film_id, f.rating, COUNT(i.inventory_id) AS copies FROM film f JOIN inventory i ON i.film_id = f.film_id GROUP BY f.film_id, f.rating), stats AS (SELECT film_id, rating, copies, AVG(copies) OVER (PARTITION BY rating) AS rating_avg_copies, AVG(copies) OVER () AS overall_avg_copies FROM film_copies) SELECT film_id, rating, copies, copies - rating_avg_copies AS diff_from_rating_avg, copies - overall_avg_copies AS diff_from_overall_avg FROM stats ORDER BY diff_from_overall_avg DESC LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: Films with no inventory copies are excluded by the inner join, so both the rating-level and overall averages are taken only over films with at least one copy.
The rating average is the mean of per-film copy counts within each rating, and the overall average is the mean of per-film copy counts across all included films, as the request specifies.
The database is MySQL 8.0+ or another engine supporting CTEs and window functions, since the schema uses MySQL-style types.
